12/14 - Comics if you're sad. Comics if you're glad. Comics don't give a shit about your feelings and they're fucking rad.

Batgirl & the Birds of Prey #5: I'm really digging this series so far. It's going back to a much more pre-Flashpoint Birds of Prey rather than the godawful New 52 Birds of Prey series. And after years of being abused by Cameron Stewart and Brenden Fletcher, I had forgotten just how great of a character Barbara Gordon is.

Detective Comics #945: Best Batman title right now and that includes All-Star Batman. A team of misfits put together by Batman and led by a hardass Batwoman, it's absolutely fantastic.

Batman/TMNT Adventures: As good as the DC Batman/TMNT crossover was, the first issue of the IDW crossover of the Animated universe was so much better. I'm probably biased from the number of times I've watched every episode and movie of the Batman Animated series (including Batman Beyond), but I don't care, it was awesome.

Silk #15: Yeah, I'm totally done with this title once the Clone Conspiracy ends (which is utterly fantastic, by the way, I normally read all my Transformers comics first, but this month I read all the Spider-man titles first). But Silk hasn't done anything in a while that has really made me care about the character. (I'm bailing on Spider-Gwen too since they keep shifting her over into Earth-616 from Earth-65 and she never meets up with Peter Parker-616. The Clone Conspiracy writer even calls out Spider-Gwen on that bullshit too.)

Amazing Spider-man: Renew Your Vows #2: Solid first issue. I can't help but feel like Marvel looked at the success of the Secret Wars mini-series and the DC Lois and Clark series (which brought back Pre-Flashpoint Superman into the New 52 universe) and thought it was a great idea. Heck, they may even kill off Peter Parker-616 and replace him with the Renew Your Vows trio (which would be awkward for Mary Jane-616). I'd be surprisingly okay with this is this is what it would take to have Peter and MJ married again.

Transformers: Lost Light #1 & Optimus Prime #1: New Transformers series (RIP Transformers and More than Meets the Eye series), but they still have the same writers from the two previous series, so there's every reason to expect the same great stuff month after month.

No IvX for me, and even @fricknmaniac seems to be passing it up. Actually, as you will see in my list, it looks like I might be dropping Marvel from my list entirely in the next few weeks.

 --------

Red Sonja #0 - I read an interview with Amy Chu and it actually made me nervous about this series. It's Red Sonja in the modern world, but the author made a comment about Sonja only learning 4 English words. It's available on the Dynamite forums. The interview made me worried that she's writing Sonja to just be a dumb brute.

Rockstars #1 - This one just seems like an interesting book. One of the ones that's more for the entertainment than the rich story. It got good reviews from those who got early versions. Here is the synopsis, "When a pattern of unsolved 'groupie' murders from the 1970s resumes in present-day Los Angeles, nobody makes the connection except Jackie Mayer, a rock nerd with a strange connection to music's urban legends and lost history. Together with muckraking music writer Dorothy Buell, they soon uncover a vast conspiracy involving a legendary band, demonic possession, and sacrifices to the dark gods of rock."

Reborn #3 - I've really been enjoying this book. Mark Millar and Greg Capullo working together. Some have complained about Capullo's art, but now that the story is journeying into the evil parts of the planet, I expect those people will be silenced when Capullo is back to drawing 'dark' images.

Cinderella Serial Killer Princess #1 - Admittedly purchased as a guilty pleasure. Looks to be a very silly story. I am mostly interested to see if Zenescope let's Cinderella kill Robyn Hood, considering they have been making sure that character stays relevant for the sake of hopefully becoming a television show.

Jessica Jones #3 - And here we are. Marvel's Jessica Jones. A series that had the most boring first two issues I may have ever read. Luke Cage is trying to find his daughter, who Jessica has hidden with her mother. She just got out of prison for some reason. The Champions (Marvel NOW!) make and appearance, another series that doesn't appeal to me. I'll give it this last shot to get the story going, but if it doesn't have a direction this week, I'll probably drop it.

Moonshine #3 - To counter the lackluster interest in Jessica Jones, we have Moonshine #3, which just happens to be a series with the BEST first two issues I have read in a long time. It takes place during prohibition in America, there is a mob boss who wants to get hooch from a backwoods bumpkin because it is the best in the country, unfortunately for him the hillbilly's aren't simple pushovers. Beautifully drawn, fantastically written. Brian Azarello and Eduardo Risso have done an incredible job so far. Very excited.

I had not heard of Rockstars at all. That actually looks like it could be real good. Please let me know how it is.

Also glad to hear about Moonshine. That's been one I have been keeping my eye on to pick up in trades.
